title: Model Choice Scenario Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Evaluation activity in which learners recommend a chat interface, a hosted API, or a local open-weight model for each of eight illustrative research scenarios and name the deciding factor. Each recommendation gets one attempt with immediate feedback and a reason; the run ends with a score out of 8, a mastery statement at 6 of 8, and the misconception exposed by each missed scenario.

educational.topic: Choosing an access path for a language model in research work
learningObjectives: Recommend one of three access paths, chat interface, hosted API, or local open-weight model, for each of eight research scenarios, with at least 6 of 8 recommendations matching the reasoning in the chapter
Name the single deciding factor for each recommendation: privacy or data policy, scale and automation, reproducibility over time, or capability and effort
prerequisites: Chat interface, API access, token cost, latency, and rate limit
Open-weight model, local model, and model version drift

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML selects and buttons reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and check or X symbols as well as a blue/orange color-blind-safe palette; all body text is 16 px.

controls.label: Access path
controls.purpose: Chooses Chat interface, Hosted API, or Local open-weight model for the current scenario. Disabled after Submit.

controls.label: Deciding factor
controls.purpose: Chooses Privacy or data policy, Scale and automation, Reproducibility over time, or Capability and effort. Feedback only; not scored. Disabled after Submit.

controls.label: Submit
controls.purpose: Commits the single attempt for the current scenario. Enabled only when both an access path and a deciding factor are chosen.

controls.label: Next Scenario / See Score
controls.purpose: Enabled after Submit. Advances to the next scenario, and after scenario 8 shows the score summary.

controls.label: More Missed Scenarios
controls.purpose: Shown only on the summary when the missed-scenario list does not fit on one page; pages through it.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Scenario-based recommendation with one attempt per item, immediate explanatory feedback, and misconception-linked review of misses
keyQuestions: Which access path would you recommend, and why?
Can the data leave the site?
Must the task run over many inputs from a script?
Must the result be reproducible with the identical model years from now?
commonMisconceptions: A local model is always the safest or cheapest choice.
The strongest hosted model is the right choice for every task.
A chat interface is adequate for any task because the model is the same.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score of at least 6 of 8 access paths matching the answer key is evidence of mastery
Comparison of the named deciding factor with the factor the reasoning turns on (not scored)
Learner explains each missed scenario using the misconception it exposes
